text: Unicode UAX #57 documents Egyptian hieroglyph code points, names, Gardiner-based identifiers, functions, and the Unikemet database. Treat Unicode identity as a sign-encoding reference, not by itself as a complete dictionary or translation.

source: Unicode Technical Note 32 — Manuel de Codage mapping
text: Unicode Technical Note 32 describes mappings between Manuel de Codage notation and Unicode Egyptian hieroglyph code points. Use it to normalize MdC, Gardiner identifiers, and Unicode glyphs before retrieval.

The Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae is an open-access publication platform for Egyptian-language texts and linked vocabulary across language stages, including Demotic. Dictionary meanings and corpus examples should be kept separate from modern cultural interpretation.

Ramses Online provides searchable annotated Egyptian texts, especially useful for Late Egyptian language, historical names, and examples in context. Record the text identifier and edition when ingesting excerpts.

Digital Egypt for Universities is a higher-education teaching resource covering Egyptian history, archaeology, language, religion, objects, and sites. Use it for explanatory background and educational summaries, with the page URL retained as provenance.

source: The Metropolitan Museum of Art — Heilbrunn Timeline
text: The Heilbrunn Timeline provides curator-authored essays, chronologies, and object context. Use museum essays for art history and cultural context, not as a replacement for a language dictionary.
JSesh documentation explains hieroglyphic typesetting and Manuel de Codage workflows. Use it to parse sign placement and encoding, while preserving the original MdC string in metadata.
